#' SAFTE Epoch Table
#'
#' This function takes the raw, properly formatted data uploaded by the user and
#' creates tables of the 1 minute Epoch data. This is the first essential step
#' for using the SAFTE model.
#'
#' Properly formatted data at a minimum has a single column for
#' sleep identification, a single column for start datetimes for bedtime, and a
#' single column for end dateimes for waketimes. It can also include work, test,
#' and crewing identified periods within the same columns.
#'
#' This is not for EPOCH by EPOCH data or data already divided into 1 minute
#' epochs.
#'
#' @param dataset Name of the properly formatted dataset uploaded into the R environment by the user (Required)
#' @param subject_id Identifier of the subject/participant/patient. (Required)
#' @param obs_start Oberservation start time (i.e. beginning of the study). Formatted as 'YYYY-mm-dd HH:MM' (Required)
#' @param obs_end Observation end time (i.e. end of the study). Cannot be more than 21 days from the obs_start. Formatted as 'YYYY-mm-dd HH:MM' (Required)
#' @param sleep_id Marker ID for a sleep period (usually "Sleep" or "sleep"). Defaults to "Sleep"
#' @param work_id Marker ID for a work period. Defaults to "Work"
#' @param crewing_id Marker ID for a crewing period within a work period. Defaults to "Crewing"
#' @param test_id Marker ID for a test period (i.e. PVT taken or medication given). Defaults to "Test"
#'
#' @returns A list 4 tables. One for identified periods of sleep, work, testing, and/or crewing if applicable. Period types not identified will return a table as Null.
#'
#' @import tidyverse
#' @import lubridate
#'
#' @export


SAFTE_epoch_tbl<-
  function(dataset,
           subject_id,
           obs_start,
           obs_end,
           sleep_id = "Sleep",
           work_id = "Work",
           crewing_id = "Crewing",
           test_id = "Test") {

  #Turn subject ID into a string--this is so a mix of numerical and alpha-char can be used together
  subject_id<-as.character(subject_id)

  #Check date formats--this will be phased out in the future
  if(is.na(ymd_hm(obs_start))) stop("Date Format Incorrect. Dates needs to be formated 'YYYY-mm-dd HH:MM'")
  if(is.na(ymd_hm(obs_end))) stop("Date Format Incorrect. Dates need to be formated 'YYYY-mm-dd HH:MM'")


  #change observation start and end from character to datetimes types
  obs_start<-ymd_hm(obs_start)
  obs_end<-ymd_hm(obs_end)

  #Check observation length to be less than 21 days
  if(difftime(obs_end,obs_start, units = "days")>21) stop("Observation period is too long, must be less than 21 days")

  #create a table of 1 minute epochs from observation start to observation end of table
  smap_obs<-tibble(ID = as.character(subject_id),
                   Obs_DateTime = map2(obs_start,
                                       obs_end,
                                       seq,
                                       by = "1 mins")) %>%
    unnest(cols = Obs_DateTime) %>%
    distinct

  #create a table of 1 minute epochs of sleep events from dataset
  smap_sleep<- dataset %>%
    mutate(ID = as.character(ID)) %>%
    filter(ID == subject_id, Event==sleep_id) %>%
    transmute(ID, Obs_DateTime = map2(Start,
                                      End,
                                      seq,
                                      by = "1 mins")) %>%
    unnest(cols = Obs_DateTime) %>%
    distinct %>%
    mutate(Sleep = 1)

  #create a table of 1 minute epochs of work events from dataset
  smap_work<- dataset %>%
    mutate(ID = as.character(ID)) %>%
    filter(ID == subject_id, Event==work_id) %>%
    transmute(ID, Obs_DateTime = map2(Start,
                                      End,
                                      seq,
                                      by = "1 mins")) %>%
    unnest(cols = Obs_DateTime) %>%
    distinct %>%
    mutate(Work = 1)

  #create a table of 1 minute epochs of test events from dataset
  smap_test<- dataset %>%
    mutate(ID = as.character(ID)) %>%
    filter(ID == subject_id, Event==test_id) %>%
    transmute(ID, Obs_DateTime = map2(Start,
                                      End,
                                      seq,
                                      by = "1 mins")) %>%
    unnest(cols = Obs_DateTime) %>%
    distinct %>%
    mutate(Test = 1)

  #create a table of 1 minute epochs of crewing events from dataset
  smap_crewing<- dataset %>%
    mutate(ID = as.character(ID)) %>%
    filter(ID == subject_id, Event==crewing_id) %>%
    transmute(ID, Obs_DateTime = map2(Start,
                                      End,
                                      seq,
                                      by = "1 mins")) %>%
    unnest(cols = Obs_DateTime) %>%
    distinct %>%
    mutate(Crewing = 1)


  #Trim the data so it begins with the first epoch of sleep. The SAFTE model can
  ###  only accurately calculate efficiency after accounting for sleep


  first_sleep <- smap_sleep$Obs_DateTime[1]

  smap_obs<-smap_obs %>%
    filter(Obs_DateTime>=first_sleep)

  #join the tables together and replace NA w/ 0 for sleep, add Epochs #,
  Sleep_EBE<-left_join(smap_obs, smap_sleep, by = c("ID", "Obs_DateTime")) %>%
    mutate(Sleep = replace_na(Sleep, 0),
           Epochs = row_number()-1,
           Time = hour(Obs_DateTime) + (minute(Obs_DateTime)/60),
           Days = as.numeric(abs(as.Date(obs_start)-as.Date(Obs_DateTime)) + 1),
           Fraction_Days = (Days + Time/24) - 1
    )

  #join the tables together and replace NA w/ 0 for wake, add Epochs #, if no work
  ###  markers are observed than table is NUll

  if(nrow(smap_work)>1){
    Work_EBE<-left_join(smap_obs, smap_work, by = c("ID", "Obs_DateTime")) %>%
      mutate(Work = replace_na(Work, 0),
             Epochs = row_number()-1,
             Time = hour(Obs_DateTime) + (minute(Obs_DateTime)/60),
             Days = as.numeric(abs(as.Date(obs_start)-as.Date(Obs_DateTime)) + 1),
             Fraction_Days = (Days + Time/24) - 1
      )
  }else{
    Work_EBE<-NULL
  }

  #join the tables together and replace NA w/ 0 for wake, add Epochs #, if no test
  ###  markers are observed than table is NUll

  if(nrow(smap_test)>1){
    Test_EBE<-left_join(smap_obs, smap_test, by = c("ID", "Obs_DateTime")) %>%
      mutate(Test = replace_na(Test, 0),
             Epochs = row_number()-1,
             Time = hour(Obs_DateTime) + (minute(Obs_DateTime)/60),
             Days = as.numeric(abs(as.Date(obs_start)-as.Date(Obs_DateTime)) + 1),
             Fraction_Days = (Days + Time/24) - 1
      )
  }else{
    Test_EBE<-NULL
  }

  #join the tables together and replace NA w/ 0 for crewing, add Epochs #, if no
  ###  crewing makers are observed than table is NUll

  if(nrow(smap_crewing)>1){
    Crewing_EBE<-left_join(smap_obs, smap_crewing, by = c("ID", "Obs_DateTime")) %>%
      mutate(Test = replace_na(Crewing, 0),
             Epochs = row_number()-1,
             Time = hour(Obs_DateTime) + (minute(Obs_DateTime)/60),
             Days = as.numeric(abs(as.Date(obs_start)-as.Date(Obs_DateTime)) + 1),
             Fraction_Days = (Days + Time/24) - 1
      )
  }else{
    Crewing_EBE<-NULL
  }

  ### Create output in a list to be referenced for future analysis

  EBE_Data<-list(Sleep_EBE = Sleep_EBE, Work_EBE = Work_EBE, Test_EBE = Test_EBE,
                 Crewing_EBE = Crewing_EBE)

  return(EBE_Data)

}

"""Compare the draft loop with SAFTEr output (R run in /tmp/ericfast/cmp/safter_out.csv).

SAFTEr's code is not copied; only its output CSV is read. Settings are matched to
SAFTEr's documented constants so structure, not parameter choices, is compared.
Usage: python3 -I compare_safter.py [safter_out.csv]
"""
import csv, math, sys
sys.path.insert(0, ".")
from recovered_loop import Params, simulate

path = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "/tmp/ericfast/cmp/safter_out.csv"

start_hour = float(rows[0]["Time"])
matched = Params(

    sleep_freeze=0, slow_recovery=True,
)

EOF

cd ~/DEV/sleep-scheduler && git pull -q 2>&1 | tail -1; cp /tmp/ericfast/cmp/run_safter.R research/fast_recon/run_safter.R && cat >> research/fast_recon/SAFTER-COMPARISON.md <<'EOF'

## Numeric run (2026-10-11)

SAFTEr's real R code (`SAFTE_epoch_tbl` + `SAFTE_model`, cloned to `/tmp`, not committed) was run with R 4.6.1 on one synthetic week: three nights 23:00-07:00, three nights 03:00-07:00, one recovery night 22:00-08:00 (9,421 one-minute epochs). The same sleep/wake minutes were fed to the draft. `run_safter.R` makes the R output; `compare_safter.py` reads it and compares. Both are in this folder (`run_safter.R` sources SAFTEr's files by path and contains none of its code).

**Draft with settings matched to SAFTEr** (a1 7.8, divisor 0.967, initial reservoir 2400, no 5-minute freeze, slow recovery on):

| Measure | Result |
|---|---|
| Reservoir, max difference over 9,421 minutes | 1.2 (on a 1956 to 2880 range) |
| Reservoir, mean difference | 0.15 |
| Effectiveness, mean difference | 0.06 points |
| Effectiveness, max difference | 3.97 points |
| Minutes with an effectiveness gap above 0.5 | 271 of 9,421, **all within the first 69 minutes awake** |

content.text:
I ran SAFTEr's real R code and my draft on the same sleep week. With matched settings they agree very closely.

**What I ran**
- I installed R 4.6.1 with Homebrew. I built the needed R packages in a private folder, `/tmp/ericfast/rlib`.
- The test week had three normal nights, three 4-hour nights, and one recovery night. That is 9,421 minutes.
- I set my draft's settings to match SAFTEr's, then compared minute by minute.

**Results with matched settings**
- **Reservoir:** The largest gap in the whole week is 1.2, on a range of about 1,956 to 2,880. The average gap is 0.15.
- **Effectiveness:** The average gap is 0.06 points. The largest gap is 3.97 points.
- **Where the gaps are:** All 271 minutes with a gap above 0.5 fall in the first 69 minutes after waking. That is where the sleep-inertia formulas differ. Right after waking, my draft's inertia is about −0.65 and SAFTEr's is about −0.001.
- So the reservoir, circadian, performance, and slow-recovery math agree with the maker's own code. Sleep inertia is the only real mismatch.

**Results with the binary's own settings**
- The reservoir differs from SAFTEr by up to 157, and effectiveness by up to 7 points.
- The cause is the parameter choices: the starting reservoir (2530 vs 2400), and whether slow recovery is on.
- Which settings FAST really used is still unknown.

**What this means:** It supports the recovered structure being right. It does not prove the draft matches FAST. We still have no FAST output to compare against, and the 7.0 vs 7.8 and 0.9677 vs 0.967 differences stay open. Draft numbers are still not FAST output.

**Where things are:** The results are in `research/fast_recon/SAFTER-COMPARISON.md`. The harness is `run_safter.R` and `compare_safter.py`, in the same folder. I updated `docs/STATUS.md` and pushed to `main` (commit 8bb7804). I copied no SAFTEr code. R and the packages stay installed on this Mac.

**Your call**
1. **Stop here.** The draft is now checked against the one public implementation we can reach. I would go with this one.
2. **Get real FAST output for one schedule.** This is the only step left that could prove the draft matches FAST. It needs a working FAST copy or a trial of the vendor's tool.

I could not run FAST here, so I did not get real FAST output.

**Why**
- **Wine** is the usual way to run Windows programs on a Mac. Homebrew disabled its Wine package on 2026-09-01, because it fails the macOS Gatekeeper check. Building Wine from source is a very large job.
- **A virtual machine app** such as UTM or Parallels is not installed. A VM would also need a Windows disk image and a Windows license. I have neither.
- **Driving the app by hand:** Even if it ran, FAST is a Windows screen app. I would have to click through it without a proper screen-control tool.
- **Your repo's rules:** Your notes say nothing from the FAST archive has been run or installed. I did not change that.

**What I could still do**
The archive already holds real FAST results. The `payload` folder has three sample schedules: `8 hrs standard schedule.fas`, `Counter-Clockwise Rotation-sample.fas`, and `Sample Train Operator.fas`. The archive also has about 21 screenshots of FAST graphs and the case-study PDFs. I could read effectiveness values off those graphs and compare them with my draft. That is rough, and many inputs are hidden, so it would only show whether the draft is in the right range. Each file also has to come down from Drive through Chrome one at a time.

**Your call**
1. **Compare against the archive screenshots and PDFs (my pick).** It is rough, but I can do it now with no new software.
2. **Get real output another way.** For example, run FAST on any Windows PC you control, or ask the vendor, the Institutes for Behavior Resources, for a sample output. You would have to do that, not me.

content.text:
Yes, new screenshots from FAST sessions would help a lot. They are better than the old archive ones, because you can set the inputs yourself. I will wait for yours and not dig through Drive.

**Best case: a text export**
- If FAST can export numbers, use that. The program has an ASCII export (a procedure called `SaveAscii`). A minute-by-minute table of effectiveness beats any graph.
- Send that file if you can get one.

**If screenshots only, capture a simple schedule**

Use a plain schedule, not a football week. It should be easy to read.
1. **Sleep and work times.** Capture the schedule grid so every sleep and work block is readable. A simple pattern works best, for example 8 hours of sleep every night for 3 nights, then 4 hours for 3 nights.
2. **Model Parameters window.** Capture the whole dialog, so I can see which values were live. In particular, I need the sleep max (3.4 or 4.4) and the feedback value.
3. **Effectiveness graph.** Capture it with the time axis and percent axis readable. Zoom in on one day if you can.
4. **Settings that change the answer.** Capture the Slow Recovery checkbox, the sleep-environment choice (Poor, Fair, Good, Excellent), and any automatic phase shift or AutoSleep setting.
5. **The same schedule twice.** Run it once with the defaults. Run it again after you change one thing, for example cut one night's sleep from 8 hours to 4. Two runs show how the curve responds.

**Where to save them**
- Put them in a folder outside your repo, for example `~/Downloads/fast-shots/`. Your repo rules keep staff and team schedules out of Git.
- Tell me the folder when they are there.

**Hook failures:** the earlier hook failures are still in `~/.claude/global-memory/transcripts/.errors.log`. I have not touched them.

**What I did meanwhile:** nothing new. The repo is unchanged since commit 8bb7804.

"""The staff CSV format: one week's itinerary in, one game weekend out.

Staff type the itinerary the way operations publishes it: a settings block,
then one row per item with a day and clock times. The confirmed decisions set
the anchoring, so there is no column for it. A kickoff offset (``K-4:15``) is
kickoff-anchored; a clock time before game day stays on the clock (Friday); a
clock time on game day or later becomes an offset from this file's kickoff
(Saturday follows kickoff). Curfew and wake-up rows become night markers, never
events. The full format is in SLEEP-SCHEDULER-SPEC.md, "Staff CSV format".

Import refuses what the model would otherwise accept silently: an unknown kind
(the model counts it as an obligation), a zero-length obligation, a duplicate
id, a night bounded twice or not at all. Every bad row is reported at once.
"""

import csv
import io
import re
from dataclasses import dataclass
from datetime import date, datetime, timedelta

    ClockTime,

)

3:Status: Release 1 design confirmed with the user on September 15, 2026, through the design interview recorded below. The calendar core, opportunity calculation, and the game-weekend model (Package 1b) are implemented on branch `worktree-calendar-core` (see `docs/STATUS.md`); CSV input (Package 2) is implemented (see "Staff CSV format"), and so is the one-page HTML comparison (Package 3, `--html`). Research basis: [FAST modernization research](FAST-MODERNIZATION-RESEARCH.md). No physiological model has been implemented or validated.
4-
5-## Product objective
6-
7-Help Applied Performance compare feasible Baylor football game-weekend schedules that protect sleep opportunities around practice, meetings, travel, and competition. Provide a reproducible explanation of each difference. Add fatigue predictions through an explicitly identified model only after its capabilities and evidence have been evaluated.
8-
9-The decisions Release 1 supports are:
10-
11-- **Friday practice and meeting times** relative to Saturday's kickoff.
12-- **Departure times** for road games, outbound and post-game (the late return).
13-
14-The first complete workflow is a Friday comparison before an early road kickoff: build a baseline game weekend from a kickoff-band template; duplicate it; move Friday practice or meeting times; compare per-night opportunity and conflicts; export a one-page comparison. Use synthetic data for development. Historical football schedules become fixtures only after staff verifies their interpretation.
15-
16-## Release 1 design decisions (interview, 2026-09-15)
17-
18-| # | Decision | Settled answer |
19-|---|---|---|
20-| Q1/Q16 | Decision the app improves | Friday practice/meeting timing against Saturday kickoff, and road-game departures including the late return. First working example: Friday times before an early road kickoff. |
21-| Q2 | Forecasting | Sleep opportunity only. An engine is expected later; not a FAST replacement until then. |
22-| Q3/Q12/Q19 | Who is modelled | One group per scenario: the travel party (road) or the full roster (home). No subgroups, no individual athlete data, no non-travel reporting in Release 1. |
23-| Q4 | Operation | Applied Performance creates and interprets; coaches and operations review the one-page comparison and decide. Athletes are not users. |
24-| Q5 | Scenario unit | One game weekend, Thursday evening through Sunday midday. Road games and home games with a Friday team hotel. Neutral-site games are road games (confirmed 2026-09-16). |
25-| Q6 | Kickoff anchoring | Game-related events are stored as offsets from kickoff; changing kickoff re-flows them. Comparing kickoff slots = duplicate and change kickoff. Amended 2026-09-16: Friday curfew, practice, and meetings are clock times chosen per week; kickoff drives Saturday. |
26-| Q7 | Movable levers | Departures, Friday practice, and meeting times. Kickoff is fixed. Post-game is fixed too (confirmed 2026-09-16: media obligations, players changing, equipment collection), so a road departure cannot move earlier by shortening it. |
27-| Q10 | Sunday | Player off day. No lift on Sunday (lifts are Monday and Wednesday). Confirmed 2026-09-16: Sunday is not planned beyond the medical check-in, so Sunday is not a lever. Enter the check-in as a `Sun` row; it bounds Saturday night only if it falls before the assumed wake. |
28-| Q11 | Sleep window rule | Rule-proposed per night from explicit practice times, practice lead time before kickoff, curfew, and meeting times (see "Protected sleep window rule"). |
29-| Q13/Q18 | Templates | Same timeline shape each week, timing varies with kickoff: three kickoff-band templates. |
30-| Q14 | Target | One editable target for all nights. |
31-| Q17 | Saturday night | Ends at an editable assumed wake time, labelled as an assumption. |
32-| Q9 | Input and output | CSV template shaped like the operations itinerary in; printable one-page HTML comparison out. |
33-| Q15 | Deployment | Local on the Applied Performance laptop. No hosting, login, or roles. |
34-
35-Values still needed from staff (data, not decisions): real itineraries per kickoff band. Fixtures use visibly synthetic values.
36-
37-**Assumption set for real weekends (decided 2026-09-16; Eric deferred the call to the assistant, evidence below).**
38-
39-| Assumption | Value | Basis |
40-|---|---|---|
41-| Sleep opportunity target | **9 h** per night | Athletes' actigraphy sleep efficiency averages about 81% (Leeder et al. 2012, J Sports Sci 30:541), so 9 h in bed yields about 7.3 h asleep, just above the <7 h habitual short sleep the 2021 expert consensus flags (Walsh et al. 2021, BJSM 55:356). 8 h in bed yields about 6.5 h. A 10 h in-bed goal (Mah et al. 2011, Sleep 34:943, collegiate basketball) raised sleep from 6.7 to 8.5 h; treat 10 h as the stretch, not the floor. |
42-| Wind-down buffer (`pre_bed_minutes`) | 30 min | Practitioner default; no study sets it. Unchanged. |
43-| Release to bed (`release_to_bed_minutes`) | **60 min** | Covers leaving the facility or stadium, travel home, eating and showering. Raised from 45: bedtime after evening competition is delayed well beyond logistics (arousal, caffeine, soreness), so 45 min understated the cost of a late release even as a logistics-only figure. |
--
107:## Staff CSV format (Package 2, 2026-09-16)
108-
109-One CSV holds one week's itinerary and becomes one game weekend (the same inputs a game-weekend JSON file stores). The CLI accepts `.csv` or `.json` for either side of a comparison. Staff never type IANA zones in rows and never edit JSON.
110-
111-**Settings block.** The file opens with a `setting,value` header row and one setting per row, then a blank row, then the itinerary table.
112-
113-| Setting | Required | Meaning |
114-|---|---|---|
115-| `id`, `title` | yes | Scenario id and report title |
116-| `kickoff` | yes | `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM`, local to `kickoff_at` |
117-| `kickoff_at` | no (`away`) | `home` or `away` |
118-| `home_zone`, `game_zone` | yes | IANA zones (a home game uses the same zone twice) |
119-| `game_type` | yes | `road` or `home`; neutral site is `road` |
120-| `source` | yes | Where the times came from |
121-| `sleep_target_hours`, `pre_bed_minutes`, `morning_minutes`, `assumptions_source` | yes | The assumption set |
122-| `saturday_night_wake`, `release_to_bed_minutes` | no | Assumed wake time; release-to-bed time for a night without a curfew |
123-
124-**Itinerary table.** Header `kind,day,start,end,title,at,arrive_at,movable,releases,id`, one row per item.
125-
126-- `kind`: `practice`, `meeting`, `walkthrough`, `meal`, `travel`, `game`, `treatment`, `lift`, `class`, `media`, `other` (obligations); `optional`, `free`, `unstructured` (ignored, e.g. "treatment available"); `curfew`, `wake-up` (night markers, never events). Any other kind is refused: the model treats unknown kinds as obligations, so a typo would silently block sleep.
127-- `day`: `Thu`, `Fri`, `Sat`, `Sun` (full names accepted), counted around the kickoff date on the stadium clock.
128-- `start`, `end`: a clock time `HH:MM` on `day`, or a kickoff offset `K-4:15` / `K+3:45` / `K` (no `day` needed). An `end` clock time earlier than `start` is the next day. Excel's `10:45:00` and `10:45 AM` forms are accepted, as is a cp1252-encoded file. The `game` row must start at `kickoff`; a mismatch is refused. An obligation needs an end after its start; enter a breakfast as its check-in with a 5–10 minute duration. Curfew and wake-up rows have no end.
129-- **Anchoring follows the confirmed decisions, with no column for it.** Kickoff offsets are kickoff-anchored. A clock time before game day stays a clock time (Friday). A clock time on game day or later is converted to an offset from this file's kickoff (Saturday follows kickoff).
130-- `at`, `arrive_at`: `home` or `away` (default `home`); `arrive_at` only on travel legs that change zone.
131-- `movable`: `yes`/`no`; blank means yes for `practice`, `meeting`, `travel` (the Q7 levers) and no otherwise.
132-- `releases`: `yes` on the obligation whose end starts a night with no curfew (the bus back to the facility; the game at home).
133-- `id`: optional; blank becomes `<day>-<title>`. Ids tie a candidate's rows to the baseline's, so keep them when editing a copy; duplicates are refused.
134-
135-**Nights.** A curfew row bounds the night of its evening; a wake-up row ends the night before it; a `releases` row starts the night its end falls in. Nights are named `thu`/`fri`/`sat` and ordered by date. Refused: a night with a wake-up but no curfew or release, a night with both, or a curfew and wake-up in different places. No Thursday rows means no Thursday night.
136-
137-**Import validation** reports every bad row at once, by row number.
138-
139-**Export** writes a weekend back to this format: clock rows before game day, kickoff offsets on game day and after, every `id` and `movable` filled in. A weekend with staff window overrides or extra clock events is refused rather than exported lossily. Round trip: events, anchoring, and zones unchanged.
140-
141-**Comparing kickoff slots.** Export with `python -m sleep_scheduler export <weekend> <out.csv>` (or write) Saturday rows as `K` offsets and change `kickoff` in the copy: the Saturday rows re-flow and Friday stays put. Retyping Saturday clock times against a new kickoff describes a different schedule, and every Saturday row is then reported as moved.
142-
143-**Real itineraries** filled into this format stay on Drive. The repo ignores `itineraries/` so a working copy cannot be committed by accident; fixtures are synthetic.

107:## Staff CSV format (Package 2, 2026-09-16)
108-
109-One CSV holds one week's itinerary and becomes one game weekend (the same inputs a game-weekend JSON file stores). The CLI accepts `.csv` or `.json` for either side of a comparison. Staff never type IANA zones in rows and never edit JSON.
110-
111-**Settings block.** The file opens with a `setting,value` header row and one setting per row, then a blank row, then the itinerary table.
112-
113-| Setting | Required | Meaning |
114-|---|---|---|
115-| `id`, `title` | yes | Scenario id and report title |
116-| `kickoff` | yes | `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM`, local to `kickoff_at` |
117-| `kickoff_at` | no (`away`) | `home` or `away` |
118-| `home_zone`, `game_zone` | yes | IANA zones (a home game uses the same zone twice) |
119-| `game_type` | yes | `road` or `home`; neutral site is `road` |
120-| `source` | yes | Where the times came from |
121-| `sleep_target_hours`, `pre_bed_minutes`, `morning_minutes`, `assumptions_source` | yes | The assumption set |
122-| `saturday_night_wake`, `release_to_bed_minutes` | no | Assumed wake time; release-to-bed time for a night without a curfew |
123-
124-**Itinerary table.** Header `kind,day,start,end,title,at,arrive_at,movable,releases,id`, one row per item.
125-
126-- `kind`: `practice`, `meeting`, `walkthrough`, `meal`, `travel`, `game`, `treatment`, `lift`, `class`, `media`, `other` (obligations); `optional`, `free`, `unstructured` (ignored, e.g. "treatment available"); `curfew`, `wake-up` (night markers, never events). Any other kind is refused: the model treats unknown kinds as obligations, so a typo would silently block sleep.
127-- `day`: `Thu`, `Fri`, `Sat`, `Sun` (full names accepted), counted around the kickoff date on the stadium clock.
128-- `start`, `end`: a clock time `HH:MM` on `day`, or a kickoff offset `K-4:15` / `K+3:45` / `K` (no `day` needed). An `end` clock time earlier than `start` is the next day. Excel's `10:45:00` and `10:45 AM` forms are accepted, as is a cp1252-encoded file. The `game` row must start at `kickoff`; a mismatch is refused. An obligation needs an end after its start; enter a breakfast as its check-in with a 5–10 minute duration. Curfew and wake-up rows have no end.
129-- **Anchoring follows the confirmed decisions, with no column for it.** Kickoff offsets are kickoff-anchored. A clock time before game day stays a clock time (Friday). A clock time on game day or later is converted to an offset from this file's kickoff (Saturday follows kickoff).
130-- `at`, `arrive_at`: `home` or `away` (default `home`); `arrive_at` only on travel legs that change zone.
131-- `movable`: `yes`/`no`; blank means yes for `practice`, `meeting`, `travel` (the Q7 levers) and no otherwise.
132-- `releases`: `yes` on the obligation whose end starts a night with no curfew (the bus back to the facility; the game at home).
133-- `id`: optional; blank becomes `<day>-<title>`. Ids tie a candidate's rows to the baseline's, so keep them when editing a copy; duplicates are refused.
134-
135-**Nights.** A curfew row bounds the night of its evening; a wake-up row ends the night before it; a `releases` row starts the night its end falls in. Nights are named `thu`/`fri`/`sat` and ordered by date. Refused: a night with a wake-up but no curfew or release, a night with both, or a curfew and wake-up in different places. No Thursday rows means no Thursday night.
136-
137-**Import validation** reports every bad row at once, by row number.
138-
139-**Export** writes a weekend back to this format: clock rows before game day, kickoff offsets on game day and after, every `id` and `movable` filled in. A weekend with staff window overrides or extra clock events is refused rather than exported lossily. Round trip: events, anchoring, and zones unchanged.
140-
141-**Comparing kickoff slots.** Export with `python -m sleep_scheduler export <weekend> <out.csv>` (or write) Saturday rows as `K` offsets and change `kickoff` in the copy: the Saturday rows re-flow and Friday stays put. Retyping Saturday clock times against a new kickoff describes a different schedule, and every Saturday row is then reported as moved.
142-
143-**Real itineraries** filled into this format stay on Drive. The repo ignores `itineraries/` so a working copy cannot be committed by accident; fixtures are synthetic.

content.text:
I built the Arizona State week from your two itinerary pages. It loads and runs cleanly. The Saturday night is the big finding.

**What I built**
- `itineraries/asu-w5-baseline.csv` is a real road night game: a flight to Phoenix, a 7:35 pm Mountain kickoff, and a flight home after the game.
- It has 36 rows from your pages: Friday meetings, flight, hotel, curfew, Saturday meals, walk-throughs, game, post-game, and the return.
- I left out staff-only items. Items with no end time run to the next item, which is your own convention.
- I guessed one thing: the game ends at 10:45 pm. The page only says post-game starts at 11:00 pm.
- The file stays out of Git. `git status` shows no changes, and nothing is committed.

**What the numbers show**
- **Friday night:** 12h 30m of opportunity. Curfew is 9:30 pm Phoenix time and the wake-up call is 10:00 am.
- **Saturday night:** only **2h 30m**, which is 6h 30m below the 9-hour target. The buses reach Fudge at 5:30 am. Allowing 60 minutes to get to bed puts the window at 6:30 am, and I assumed a 9:00 am wake.
- **Not counted:** the flight itself, from 12:45 am to 5:00 am. A seat on the plane is an opportunity, not confirmed sleep. The tool also cannot account for the 2-hour time-zone change.
- **Friday clock:** The Friday window is in Phoenix time. The players' bodies are on Central time.
- **Assumed wake:** The 9:00 am Sunday wake is my assumption. Sunday is a player off day, and the real wake time could be later.

**TCU placeholders**
- I replaced two made-up times with the Arizona State pattern. The Friday curfew is now 9:30 pm. The Saturday wake-up is 8:25 am, kickoff minus 9h 35m. Both are labeled BORROWED.
- The TCU file still has made-up Thursday curfew, travel, and return times. It is still partial.

**What I did not do:** I did not run the FAST draft on the Arizona State week. No one has real sleep times for it.

**Your call**
1. **Use the Arizona State file as the baseline and test changes.** For example, move the Saturday return earlier and compare the night. I would go with this one. It is real data.
2. **Wait for the TCU travel itinerary** and finish that file first.

Yes, add the Friday–Saturday travel itineraries for several games. Skip the Monday–Thursday weekly schedule for now.

**Why Friday and Saturday**
- Your Release 1 plan covers one game weekend, Thursday evening through Sunday midday. The decisions it supports are Friday practice and meeting times, and the road departures, including the late return.
- The Arizona State pages gave me everything that plan uses: curfew, wake-up, flight, hotel, game, and the 5:30 am return.
- Your plan also says real itineraries per kickoff band are still missing. The tool uses three bands: early (before noon), afternoon (noon to 5:59 pm), and night (6 pm and later).
- Several games let us compare those patterns: the late-return problem on a road night game, how curfew and wake-up change with kickoff time, and where the biggest sleep losses are.

**Why skip Monday to Thursday for now**
- Your plan says the tool covers only the game weekend. Monday to Thursday is outside it.
- The weekly page is a staff page. The Release 1 tool models the travel party or the roster, not staff.
- The weekly page would matter later. It would matter if you pick a fatigue model, because that model needs several days of sleep history before the game.

**What I found**
- **`GAME_WEEK_ITINERARIES`:** It holds only a `2026` folder. That has the Auburn and PVAMU PDFs. There is no 2024 or 2025 folder.
- **Earlier staff schedule:** One PDF, `2022-10-08_Week7_Staff_Schedule_West_Virginia.pdf`. It is a weekly staff schedule from 2022, in a folder I did not open.
- **Bowl trip:** `2025-12-15_Travel_Itinerary_Day1` (PDF and DOCX), in a `Travel` folder. It looks like a December 2025 trip. I have not opened it.
- **Not found:** Nothing named like a 2024 or 2025 season of game-week itineraries. The PDFs may be scans or images that Drive search cannot read, or they may be named differently.

**What I need**
- The folder name, or a link to it, and I will list what is inside.

**What I will do once I find them**
- Build each game in the same CSV format as the other five games, in `itineraries/`, and keep them out of Git.
- Process only the Friday–Saturday pages, as agreed.
- Mark every guessed time as ASSUMED.
- If they are screenshots or scans, I read them the same way I read your images.

**Your call**
1. **Send the folder name or link (my pick).**
2. **Use the December 2025 travel itinerary I found.** I can open it and see if it fits as one more road case.

entries.description:
Call this tool to fetch a natural language representation of a known Drive file, and if specified, its comments.

REQUIREMENTS & WORKFLOW:
 - `fileId` is required. You MUST pass an exact Drive file ID returned by a previous discovery tool (`search_files` or `list_recent_files`) or provided explicitly in the user prompt.
 - NEVER guess, invent, or hallucinate a `fileId` string from a file title or name.
 - If given a file title, name, or topic without an explicit `fileId`, you MUST FIRST call `search_files` to find the file and retrieve its `fileId` before invoking this tool.

The file content may be incomplete for very large files. The text representation will change over time, so don't make assumptions about the particular format of the text returned by this tool. If supported and specified, comment tags will be included in the content.

Supported Mime Types:

 - `application/vnd.google-apps.document` (supports comments)
 - `application/vnd.google-apps.presentation` (supports comments)
 - `application/vnd.google-apps.spreadsheet` (supports comments)
 - `application/pdf` 
 - `application/msword` 
 - `application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document` 
 - `application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet` 
 - `application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.presentationml.presentation` 
 - `application/vnd.oasis.opendocument.spreadsheet` 
 - `application/vnd.oasis.opendocument.presentation` 
 - `application/x-vnd.oasis.opendocument.text` 
 - `image/png` 
 - `image/jpeg` 
 - `image/jpg` 

If the file is not found, try using other tools like `search_files` to find the file the user is requesting using keywords.

fileId.description: Required. The ID of the file to retrieve.

includeComments.description: Whether to include comments in the response. Comments will be inlined in the text content of the file with a mapping to the comment threads. Note: Comments are only supported for Google Docs, Slides, and Sheets.

input_schema.description: Request to read file content with support for fetching comments.

content.text:
I used both files and neither one helps. The earlier seasons are still missing.

**What each file turned out to be**
- **December 2025 travel itinerary:** It is a personal family road trip. It covers Waco to Overland Park on December 26, with a family hotel and kid stops. It is not a football trip. I read it only to check, and I used none of it. I did not save it anywhere.
- **2022 West Virginia Week 7 schedule:** It is a weekly staff schedule, not a travel itinerary. It says "See Travel Itinerary for Detailed Schedule," and that itinerary is not in the file. Its game was a Thursday night, 7:00 pm kickoff at West Virginia. It has no curfew, no wake-up, and no player times, so I cannot build a game weekend from it.

**My last search**
- I searched the PDF text for "PROTECT THE TEAM," the phrase that ends every itinerary page. It found nothing from 2024 or 2025. The hits were a 2025 presentation and some unrelated documents.
- So Drive search cannot see those pages. They may be scans, images, or saved under a name I did not try.

**What you have now:** Six real games. Five are built in `itineraries/`, plus the TCU partial. They cover every case except an early-kickoff road game. That is enough to compare changes this week.

**Your call**
1. **Run the comparison on the five games now (my pick).** Tell me which lever to move, or I pick the Arizona State return, the one real problem week.
2. **Find the earlier seasons first.** Send the folder name or link, or look in your Drive "Recent" list for a file with a date from 2024 or 2025.

zone: str,
    events: Mapping[str, Event],
    assumptions: AssumptionSet,
    override: WindowOverride | None,
) -> NightPlan:
    if marker.curfew is not None:
        start = _resolve(marker.curfew, kickoff, game_date, zone)
        start_source = "curfew"
    else:
        if assumptions.release_to_bed_minutes is None:
            raise ValueError(
                f"{marker.night} night is released by {marker.released_by} and the "
                "assumption set has no release_to_bed_minutes; set the assumed time "
                "from release to bed rather than leaving it out"
            )
        release = events[marker.released_by]
        start = release.interval.end + timedelta(minutes=assumptions.release_to_bed_minutes)
        start_source = f"release:{release.id}"

    night_date = _night_date(start, zone)
    reporting = Interval.of(
        f"{night_date.isoformat()}T{NIGHT_REPORT_START}",
        f"{(night_date + timedelta(days=1)).isoformat()}T{NIGHT_REPORT_END}",
        zone,
    )

    # A staff-set end is settled first: obligations must be judged against the
    # edge staff chose, not the wake-up call it replaced.
    if override is not None and override.end is not None:
        end, end_source = override.end.instant, "staff override"
    elif marker.wake is not None:
        end, end_source = _resolve(marker.wake, kickoff, game_date, zone), "wake-up call"
    else:
        end, end_source = _assumed_wake(night_date, zone, assumptions, marker.night), "assumed wake"

    # Only an obligation already under way at the start pushes it: meetings
    # that run past curfew, then a snack that began before the pushed start.
    # One that begins later stays inside the window, where evaluate() subtracts
    # its time and reports the conflict, rather than the night silently
    # starting after it.
    obligations = sorted(
        (event for event in events.values() if event.mandatory),
        key=lambda event: event.interval.start,
    )
    for event in obligations:
        if event.interval.start < min(start, end):
            ready = event.interval.end + assumptions.pre_bed
            if ready > start:
                start, start_source = ready, f"obligation:{event.id}"

    if override is not None and override.start is not None:
        start, start_source = override.start.instant, "staff override"

    if start >= end:
        return NightPlan(
            marker.night,
            None,
            note=f"no protected sleep window: {start_source} runs past the {end_source}",
            reporting=reporting,
        )

    window = ProtectedSleepWindow(
        id=f"{marker.night}-night",
        label=f"{marker.night.capitalize()} night",
        interval=Interval(start, end, start_zone=zone, end_zone=zone),
        kind="hotel" if marker.at == "away" else "home",
        proposed=True,
        start_source=start_source,
        end_source=end_source,
    )
    return NightPlan(marker.night, window, reporting=reporting)

content.text:
I ran the comparison on the Arizona State week. A stay-over in Phoenix beats the 5:30 am return by 3h 30m on Saturday night.

**The lever I tested:** After the game, stay in Phoenix and fly home Sunday morning. I invented the details. The bus to the hotel is 30 minutes, the wake-up call is 7:30 am, and the flight leaves at 10:45 am. This follows your plan's lever for the late return.

| | Real plan (fly home after the game) | Stay-over candidate |
|---|---|---|
| Saturday night opportunity | 2h 30m (6:30 to 9:00 am Central, home) | **6h 00m** (1:30 to 7:30 am Phoenix time) |
| Friday night | 12h 30m | 12h 30m, unchanged |
| Conflicts | none | none |

**Caveats**
- **Body clock:** Phoenix is 2 hours behind Waco, and the players' bodies stay on Central time. The stay-over window of 1:30 to 7:30 am Phoenix is 3:30 to 9:30 am Central. The gain is real, but smaller than the clock times suggest.
- **Plane time:** The real plan's flight, 12:45 to 5:00 am, is not counted as sleep opportunity.
- **My numbers:** The 7:30 am wake and the 10:45 flight are my guesses. A later flight would add more.
- **Costs not modeled:** A hotel night, equipment, the Sunday medical check-in, and staff and family plans.

**A limit I found in your tool**
- The compare command refused to put these two side by side. It says "different reporting intervals." The cause is that the night moved from Waco to a Phoenix hotel.
- That is exactly the kind of comparison Release 1 should support, so this is a gap. I worked around it by running each file alone.

**What I changed:** I added the finding to `docs/STATUS.md`, committed, and pushed to `main` (33ff5fd). No itinerary data went into Git. The new candidate file is `itineraries/asu-w5-stayover-candidate.csv`. It is local and git-ignored.

**Your call**
1. **Fix the tool so it can compare a home night against a hotel night in another time zone.** I would go with this one. It is the comparison the late-return decision needs. It is a code change, so I want your approval first.
2. **Leave it.** You can still read each file alone, as I did.

"""Per-night reporting and comparison of two game weekends.

The decision this answers: does moving Friday practice, meetings, or a
departure change sleep opportunity on any night, and did the candidate quietly
move something that is not a lever?
"""

from dataclasses import replace
from datetime import timedelta

import pytest

from sleep_scheduler.temporal import LocalTime
from sleep_scheduler.weekend import build_weekend, compare_weekends, evaluate_weekend
from synthetic import (
    ASSUMPTIONS,
    CHICAGO,
    DENVER,
    EARLY_KICKOFF,
    H,
    road_early_released_template,
    road_early_template,
)

M = timedelta(minutes=1)
MEETINGS_PAST_CURFEW = {"fri-meeting": (-13 * H, -12 * H - 10 * M)}  # 22:00-22:50 MT


RELEASE = replace(ASSUMPTIONS, release_to_bed_minutes=30)


def build(kickoff=EARLY_KICKOFF, id="baseline", assumptions=ASSUMPTIONS, template=None, **kwargs):
    return build_weekend(
        template or road_early_template(),
        kickoff,
        home_zone=CHICAGO,
        game_zone=DENVER,
        assumptions=assumptions,
        id=id,
        title=f"{id} (synthetic)",
        **kwargs,
    )


def candidate(**kwargs):
    return build(id="candidate", **kwargs)


def test_each_night_of_the_weekend_is_reported_separately():
    report = evaluate_weekend(build())
    assert [n.night for n in report.nights] == ["thu", "fri", "sat"]
    # Thu 23:00-07:00 CT, Fri 23:00-06:00 MT, Sat 23:00 CT to assumed 09:00 CT.
    assert [n.hours for n in report.nights] == [8.0, 7.0, 10.0]


def test_night_reporting_interval_is_fixed_by_date_not_by_the_proposed_window():
    base = evaluate_weekend(build()).night("fri").report.reporting_interval
    late = evaluate_weekend(candidate(offsets=MEETINGS_PAST_CURFEW)).night("fri").report.reporting_interval
    assert late == base
    assert (base.wall("start"), base.wall("end")) == ("2026-10-02T18:00", "2026-10-03T12:00")

content.text:
I fixed the compare command. It now compares a night at home with a night at an away hotel, and I pushed the change to `main` (commit 5f0f79e).

**What was wrong:** Each night's report window is fixed on that place's own clock. When a night moved from Waco to Phoenix, the two windows differed by 2 hours, and the tool refused to compare them.

**What it does now**
- It compares both nights over one shared window that covers both. If the shared window would run longer than 30 hours, it still refuses.
- It labels the change of place in the printed report. The one-page HTML report says it in the sign-off section.
- `WeekendComparison` now has a `place_changes` list.
- Nights that stay put compare exactly as before.

**The real Arizona State comparison now runs**
- **Saturday night:** 2h 30m with the real return, 6h 00m with a Phoenix stay-over. The difference is +3h 30m.
- **Friday night:** unchanged at 12h 30m.

**What I checked**
- I wrote the tests first. Three failed before the fix, as expected.
- All 214 tests pass: the old 210 plus 4 new ones.
- I added a short note to the spec, and I updated `docs/STATUS.md`.

**What it does not do:** It compares elapsed time only, not body-clock hour. A night slept two hours behind home time shows the same hours as one slept at home. The spec now says so.

**Your call**
1. **Run more lever tests on the real weeks.** For example, Friday meeting times for the Colorado early kickoff, once the Friday page arrives. I would go with this one.
2. **Stop here.** The tool and the five real baselines are ready.

"""Run one-lever candidates against real baselines in itineraries/ (git-ignored).

Each lever edits a copy of a baseline CSV and compares the result with the
original using the project's own compare_weekends. Prints per-night hour changes,
conflicts and flags. Holds no itinerary data; reads whatever is in itineraries/.

Usage (from the repo root):
    PYTHONPATH=src python3 research/lever_tests/run_levers.py
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import csv
import io
import sys
from pathlib import Path

from sleep_scheduler.itinerary_csv import weekend_from_csv
from sleep_scheduler.weekend import compare_weekends

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
BASELINES = [
    "asu-w5-baseline", "auburn-w1-baseline", "pvamu-w2-baseline",
    "latech-w3-baseline", "colorado-w4-saturday-only",
]


def split(text: str):
    head, _, table = text.partition("\n\n")
    rows = list(csv.reader(io.StringIO(table.strip())))
    return head, rows[0], [dict(zip(rows[0], r)) for r in rows[1:]]


def join(head, cols, rows) -> str:
    out = io.StringIO()
    w = csv.writer(out, lineterminator="\n")
    w.writerow(cols)
    for r in rows:
        w.writerow([r.get(c, "") for c in cols])
    return head + "\n\n" + out.getvalue()


def shift(t: str, minutes: int) -> str | None:
    if not t:
        return t
    h, m = (int(x) for x in t.split(":"))
    total = h * 60 + m + minutes
    return None if not 0 <= total < 24 * 60 else f"{total // 60:02d}:{total % 60:02d}"


def move(rows, pick, minutes):
    out, touched = [], 0
    for r in rows:
        r = dict(r)
        if pick(r):
            s, e = shift(r["start"], minutes), shift(r["end"], minutes)
            if s is not None and e is not None:
                r["start"], r["end"] = s, e
                touched += 1
        out.append(r)
    return out, touched


def hour(t):
    return int(t.split(":")[0]) if t else -1


LEVERS = {
    "Fri evening meetings +60 min": lambda rows: move(
        rows, lambda r: r["day"] == "Fri" and r["kind"] == "meeting" and r["movable"] == "yes"
        and hour(r["start"]) >= 18, 60),
    "Fri daytime movable items -60 min": lambda rows: move(
        rows, lambda r: r["day"] == "Fri" and r["movable"] == "yes" and 0 <= hour(r["start"]) < 18, -60),
    "Fri curfew +60 min": lambda rows: move(rows, lambda r: r["kind"] == "curfew" and r["day"] == "Fri", 60),
    "Sat wake-up +60 min": lambda rows: move(rows, lambda r: r["kind"] == "wake-up" and r["day"] == "Sat", 60),
}


def run(name, base_text, cand_text):
    try:
        cmp_ = compare_weekends(weekend_from_csv(base_text), weekend_from_csv(cand_text))
    except Exception as exc:  # report, do not hide
        return f"{name:<36} ERROR {type(exc).__name__}: {exc}"
    cells = []
    for night in ("fri", "sat"):
        try:
            n = cmp_.night(night)
            cells.append(f"{night} {n.hours_delta:+.2f}h (conf {len(n.baseline.conflicts)}->{len(n.candidate.conflicts)})")
        except KeyError:
            cells.append(f"{night} n/a")
    flags = f"flags {len(cmp_.flags)}" if cmp_.flags else "flags 0"
    place = " place-change" if cmp_.place_changes else ""
    return f"{name:<36} " + " | ".join(cells) + f" | {flags}{place}"


def main() -> int:
    for base in BASELINES:
        path = ROOT / "itineraries" / f"{base}.csv"
        if not path.exists():
            print(f"skip {base}: not found in itineraries/")
            continue
        text = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        head, cols, rows = split(text)
        print(f"\n== {base}")
        for name, lever in LEVERS.items():
            new_rows, touched = lever(rows)
            if not touched:
                print(f"{name:<36} (no matching rows)")
                continue
            print(run(name, text, join(head, cols, new_rows)))
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())
EOF

content.text:
I ran lever tests on the five real weeks. Almost nothing changes sleep opportunity except the road stay-over.

**The tests** each moved one thing and compared with the tool.

| Lever | Friday night | Saturday night |
|---|---|---|
| Friday daytime items 60 min earlier | 0 in all five | 0 |
| Friday evening meetings 60 min later | −0.33 to −0.58 h | 0 |
| Friday evening meetings 60 min earlier | 0 | 0 |
| Friday curfew 60 min later | −0.75 to −1.00 h | 0 |
| Friday curfew 60 min earlier | 0, except Arizona State +0.25 h | 0 |
| Saturday wake-up call 60 min later | small gain, plus a new conflict | 0 |
| **Stay over, fly home Sunday 10:45** | 0 | **Arizona State +3.5 h, Auburn +0.75 h** |

**What it means**
- **What sets Friday bedtime:** The fixed late-night snack and visualization, plus the 30-minute wind-down, put bedtime at about 9:15 to 9:45 pm. Moving meetings or the curfew earlier gains nothing. Moving meetings later only hurts when their tail crosses that bedtime.
- **Friday daytime moves:** They change nothing in any of the five weeks. Practice and meeting times have other effects, but this tool does not measure them.
- **Wake-up calls:** The wake-up call is 20 minutes before the first obligation in all five games. Moving it later creates a conflict. It does not create sleep.
- **The one real lever:** The stay-over. It helps a lot when the return is as late as Arizona State's. It helps little at Auburn, where the plane lands at 10:30 pm.

**Cautions**
- **Colorado:** Its Friday numbers are an artifact. I have no Friday page, so only the curfew binds.
- **Stay-over flags:** The stay-over runs carry one flag. The bus to Fudge is marked fixed in my files, and its time changed.
- **Stay-over guesses:** The 7:30 am wake, the 10:45 flight, and the 30-minute hotel bus are my guesses.

**What I saved:** I added `research/lever_tests/run_levers.py`, which holds no itinerary data. I also updated `docs/STATUS.md`, committed, and pushed to `main` (9b9403c). The script reads your git-ignored `itineraries/` folder.

**Your call**
1. **Test the late-snack constraint (my pick).** Ask whether the 8:35 pm snack and visualization could end earlier, since they set bedtime. That is the one lever the results point to.
2. **Stop here.** You have the finding and the script.

Moving the Friday evening block earlier works, but it would not help. Friday night already has more sleep opportunity than the 9-hour target.

**What moving the evening block earlier does**
- I moved the Friday evening meetings, the late snack, the visualization, and the curfew earlier together.
- **30 minutes earlier:** +0.5 h on Friday night, in every game.
- **60 minutes earlier:** +1.0 h on Friday night, in every game.
- The tool flags the snack and the visualization, because they are fixed items and I moved them.

**Why it would not help: each night against the 9-hour target**

| Game | Friday night | Saturday night |
|---|---|---|
| Arizona State (road, night) | 12.50 h (**+3.50**) | 2.50 h (**−6.50**) |
| Auburn (road, afternoon) | 11.25 h (+2.25) | 8.75 h (−0.25) |
| PVAMU (home, night) | 12.50 h (+3.50) | 8.50 h (−0.50) |
| LA Tech (home, afternoon) | 11.50 h (+2.50) | 12.50 h (+3.50) |
| Colorado (home, early) | 9.25 h (+0.25, artifact) | 15.00 h (+6.00) |

- **Friday:** All four full weeks sit 2.25 to 3.5 hours above target.
- **Saturday:** The short nights are Saturday. Arizona State is the real problem, at 6.5 hours short.
- **Assumptions behind the small Saturday shortfalls:** Auburn (−0.25 h) and PVAMU (−0.5 h) rest on my assumptions of a 60-minute post-game, 60 minutes to get to bed, and a 9:00 am Sunday wake. Treat those two as close to the target, not as real shortfalls.
- **Colorado:** Its Friday number is an artifact, because I have no Friday page.

**What this means:** The Friday levers don't change anything, and the Friday evening block has plenty of slack. The sleep opportunity is lost on a late return home. At Arizona State that is the 5:30 am arrival.

**What I saved:** I updated the lever script and `docs/STATUS.md`, then pushed to `main` (commit 7015efa).

**Your call**
1. **Look harder at the late return.** For example, what time the plane could leave, or what a stay-over costs in hotel and Sunday logistics. It is the only lever that matters here. I would go with this one.
2. **Stop here.** You have the full picture for these five weeks.

"""How the post-game departure delay (1 to 2 h after the game is standard) moves Saturday night.

Road games: shift the airport bus, flight and landing bus together. Home games: change
the assumed post-game length (the release-to-bed clock starts when it ends).
Reads git-ignored itineraries/. Sleep opportunity, not sleep obtained.
Usage: PYTHONPATH=src python3 research/lever_tests/departure_delay.py
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import sys
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent))
from run_levers import ROOT, join, split  # noqa: E402

from sleep_scheduler.itinerary_csv import weekend_from_csv  # noqa: E402
from sleep_scheduler.weekend import evaluate_weekend  # noqa: E402

DAYS = ["Sat", "Sun"]


def to_abs(day: str, clock: str) -> int:
    h, m = (int(x) for x in clock.split(":"))
    return DAYS.index(day) * 1440 + h * 60 + m


def from_abs(total: int) -> tuple[str, str]:
    return DAYS[total // 1440], f"{(total % 1440) // 60:02d}:{total % 60:02d}"


def shift_road(rows, delta: int):
    out = []
    for r in rows:
        r = dict(r)
        if r["id"] in ("sat-to-airport", "sat-flight", "sat-bus"):
            start = to_abs(r["day"], r["start"])
            end = to_abs(r["day"], r["end"])
            if end <= start:
                end += 1440
            r["day"], r["start"] = from_abs(start + delta)
            _, r["end"] = from_abs(end + delta)
        out.append(r)
    return out


def sat_hours(text: str) -> float:
    return evaluate_weekend(weekend_from_csv(text)).night("sat").hours


def postgame_len(rows, extra: int):
    out = []
    for r in rows:
        r = dict(r)
        if r["id"] == "sat-postgame":
            h, m = (int(x) for x in r["end"].split(":"))
            r["end"] = f"{((h * 60 + m + extra) % 1440) // 60:02d}:{(h * 60 + m + extra) % 60:02d}"
        out.append(r)
    return out


def main() -> int:
    print("Road games: depart for the airport earlier or later than the real plan (Saturday night, target 9 h)")
    for base, label in (("asu-w5-baseline", "Arizona State (real plan leaves about 1h15 after the game)"),
                        ("auburn-w1-baseline", "Auburn (real plan leaves about 1h15 after the game)")):
        path = ROOT / "itineraries" / f"{base}.csv"
        if not path.exists():
            continue
        head, cols, rows = split(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        print(f"  {label}")
        for delta, note in ((-15, "1h after game"), (0, "real plan"), (15, "1h30 after"), (45, "2h after game")):
            print(f"    {delta:+3d} min ({note:<14}): {sat_hours(join(head, cols, shift_road(rows, delta))):5.2f} h")
    print("Home games: assumed post-game length before release (the file assumes 60 min)")
    for base in ("pvamu-w2-baseline", "latech-w3-baseline", "colorado-w4-saturday-only"):
        path = ROOT / "itineraries" / f"{base}.csv"
        if not path.exists():
            continue
        head, cols, rows = split(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        cells = [f"{60 + extra:3d} min {sat_hours(join(head, cols, postgame_len(rows, extra))):5.2f} h"
                 for extra in (0, 30, 60)]
        print(f"  {base:<28} " + " | ".join(cells))
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())
EOF

This one file serves Claude Code, Codex and Cowork (uploaded to claude.ai). Cowork has no TaskList and no Claude Code memory hooks: do what applies there and say what was skipped.

## Step 1 — Loose-ends sweep

- `git status` across **every** repo in DEV, not only the ones named in this conversation. Another session, another harness, or the other machine may have left work dirty, and a closeout that only checks what it remembers touching will say "clear to sign off" over someone else's uncommitted work. Walk `DEV/`, `DEV/Football/` and `DEV/SpecialRequests/`, and report any repo with uncommitted or unpushed commits. The full walk takes about 90 seconds.
  - Windows: `git -C <repo> status --porcelain` per repo. Do NOT use `Get-ChildItem -Recurse` to look for files; it silently skips paths past the 260-character limit. Inside a repo, `git ls-files` is the reliable way to ask whether a file exists.
  - Repos with dirty state you did not touch: commit and push them like any other, and name them in the report so the user knows another session left them.
- **Registry drift.** Run `python <dir of portfolio_json>/portfolio.py crosswalk` (`portfolio_json` is in `~/.claude/skills/_shared/config.<platform>.json`). It compares `portfolio.json` with every DEV folder and Drive `01_PROJECTS` folder and only reports; it never moves anything. Do not fix drift during closeout. List each item it found under "Still open", naming any folder created this session first: that is a project started without a row, the exact way projects got lost before the 2026-10-03 organization pass. `drive_unreachable` means the Drive checks never ran; say so, do not call it clean. Cowork cannot run it; say it was skipped.
- **7-day rule.** Run `python <dir of portfolio_json>/portfolio.py seven-day --apply`. Name any project it paused, and any project on its last two days, under "Still open" with what it still needs (a receiver, step 1). Revive with the board's status pill or `portfolio.py` once there is a first step to show.
- Unfinished todos/tasks from this session (TaskList if available).
- Background jobs or workflows still running.
- Anything the user was promised earlier in the session that wasn't delivered.

## Step 2 — Commit & push

- **Registry edits get their own commit.** In project-triage, if `git status --porcelain portfolio.json` shows a change (board edits from the day, `set-status`, `set-receiver`), commit that file alone first as `data: board edits <YYYY-MM-DD>`, then the rest. The board header's "N unpushed registry edits" counts these; a skipped one becomes a JSON merge conflict when the other machine edits too.
- Every repo touched this session: stage, commit with a descriptive message, `git pull --no-rebase` (the other machine may have pushed), push. If the merge conflicts, follow the conflict steps in `dev-sync/SKILL.md` (they are the one home for them), then push and list the file under "Still open".
- Before staging, make sure any new file over 95 MB and any `.env` is in `.gitignore`.
- Local-only repos (CLAUDE.md says so): commit, do not push, list it.
- If `~/.claude/mods` changed this session (a mod added, edited or `.disabled`), run the mods sync (`bash ~/.claude/mods/mods-sync.sh` on the Mac, `powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File $HOME\.claude\mods\mods-sync.ps1` on Windows) and list any invalid mod under "Still open".
- Also check the three config repos, `~/.claude` (dotclaude), `~/.claude/skills` (claude-skills) and `~/.claude/global-memory` (claude-global-memory). If any has changes, commit and push it the same way, so the other machine's `/dev-sync` picks it up.
- **Push `global-memory` even on a light session.** `daily-backup` pushes it nightly, which is too late for a same-day handoff: work the Mac in the afternoon, sit down at Windows that evening, and anything written to MEMORY.md or handoffs is still only on the Mac. Pushing it here is what makes memory available to the other machine tonight rather than tomorrow. It is the only repo that carries memory across, so treat an unpushed `global-memory` the same as an unpushed project repo: it blocks "clear to sign off".
- Nothing to commit → say so in one line, move on.

## Step 3 — Memory verification

- Check `~/.claude/global-memory/transcripts/.errors.log` — must be empty. If not, surface contents and fix the hook issue if obvious.
- Confirm today's transcript file exists at `~/.claude/global-memory/transcripts/<today>.md` and was modified within the last few hours. On a Cowork-only day it may be absent; say so, it is not an error.
- Run the dev-docs harvest so repo docs reach memsearch: `bash ~/.claude/scripts/harvest-dev-docs.sh` (Mac) or `powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File $HOME\.claude\scripts\harvest-dev-docs.ps1` (Windows). It copies every repo's `docs/*.md` into `~/.claude/global-memory/dev-docs/`, which is on the index list. One line of output; do this after Step 4 so today's STATUS is included.
- If this session produced a durable decision or new active thread, update `~/.claude/global-memory/MEMORY.md` (respect the 2,500-char cap; consolidate before adding) or write a Tier A memory file per the memory-system rules in CLAUDE.md.
- **Tier A does not cross machines — mirror it or lose it.** Project memory lives under a slug built from the project's absolute path, and that path differs on the Mac and the Windows laptop, so a Tier A file written today is not auto-injected tomorrow on the other machine. Global memory and the repo both cross; Tier A does not. So for every Tier A fact written this session, ask: is this durable and project-scoped? If yes, it must also land in the repo — `docs/STATUS.md` for current state, `docs/DECISIONS.md` for a decision and its reasoning, the dated handoff for the detail. Treat Tier A as a fast local cache and the repo as the record. If a fact only ever exists in Tier A, assume the other machine will never see it.

## Step 4 — Cross-harness handoff

This is the **canonical durable handoff** — the one future sessions and other harnesses read. (For a mid-session, chat-only summary before `/clear`, that's the `session-handoff` skill; the mattpocock `handoff` skill writes to the OS temp dir and is not durable — don't rely on it for cross-session state.)

If real work happened this session (not just Q&A), write a handoff to
`<repo>/docs/handoffs/<YYYY-MM-DD>-<slug>.md` (or `~/.claude/global-memory/handoffs/` if no repo fits):

- What was being worked on and why
- Decisions made (with the reasoning that would be lost)
- Exact file paths of everything created or modified this session
- Next actions, most important first
- Anything mid-flight (open questions, awaited inputs)

Plain markdown, no harness-specific syntax — Codex, Antigravity, or a fresh Claude session must be able to resume from it. Commit it with the Step 2 commit when in a repo.

**Always, in every repo touched (even for light sessions): update `docs/STATUS.md`.** It is the file the next session reads first, on either machine, in any harness. Rewrite the sections in place, keep it short:

- `## Current state` — two to five lines on where things stand today
- `## Next` — most important first. Item 1 is one concrete action (a command to run or a file to open), not a theme: it is the line `~/.claude/scripts/where-was-i.py` shows Eric the next morning
- `## Open questions` — decisions waiting on Eric, each one written out in full as its own top-level bullet: the question itself and enough context to answer it without opening another file. Never a pointer ("See PLAN.md"): `/startup` reads this section across every repo with `where-was-i.py --decisions`, and a pointer gives no question to answer. Mark answered items `ANSWERED <date>: …` or strike them through (`~~…~~`) so they drop off that list. Leave the section empty, not "-", when nothing is waiting.
- `## Gotchas` — anything that will bite the next session

Then run `python ~/.claude/scripts/where-was-i.py --decisions --days 1`. It prints exactly what tomorrow's `/startup` will show as "Decisions waiting on you". Every decision this session left open must appear there as a readable question; if one is missing or shows as a pointer, fix that repo's `## Open questions` before the commit.

The dated handoff file is the detailed record; STATUS.md is the summary. Do Step 4 before the Step 2 commit so both land in the same push.

**Keep the resume cards true (PM system design Decision 9).** The live board shows each project as a card read from STATUS and the registry; if a card doesn't make sense tonight, it won't in six weeks. Run `python <dir of portfolio_json>/landed.py scan --days 1` (about a minute), then `python <dir of portfolio_json>/portfolio.py card-check`. It prints the card of every registry project touched today, on either machine, with its gaps. Fix each gap before the Step 2 commit:

- `STATUS has no entry dated <today>`: add `- <today>: <what happened>` under the repo's Done / Current state.
- `STATUS has no Next item`: put one concrete action first under `## Next`.
- `no next step (next_action)` (Drive-only row): set it on the board or with `portfolio.py add-update <name> "<note>" --next-action "<step>"`.
- `needs a receiver`: `portfolio.py set-receiver <name> "<who>"` (a name, or `me: <why>`). Ask Eric when it is not obvious from the session; never invent one.
- `touched but marked <status>`: revive it (`portfolio.py set-status <name> active`) or say in STATUS why a retired project was touched.

Re-run `card-check` after the fixes. Its output is the last section of the report (**Cards:**); trim to projects with work today if it is long, but never drop one that still has a gap.

## Step 5 — Verdict

End with a single short report:

```
## Closeout — <date>

**Committed & pushed:** <repos + one-line summary, or "nothing to commit">
**STATUS.md:** updated in <repos>
**Memory:** captured ✓ / issue found: <what> / skipped (Cowork, no hooks)
**Handoff:** <path, or "not needed — no substantive work">
**Registry drift:** <N items, or "none"> (`portfolio.py crosswalk`)
**Still open:** <numbered list, or "none">

Clear to sign off. / Not clear: <the one thing blocking>.

**Cards:** <`portfolio.py card-check` output, after the Step 4 fixes>
```

The cards come last on purpose: they are what the next session, on either machine, picks up from.

"Clear to sign off" means: every touched repo is pushed (or is a declared local-only repo). If anything is unpushed, the verdict is "Not clear" and the unpushed repo is the one thing blocking.

Every file created or modified during the session must appear somewhere in the report with its full path — "where did this save?" should never need to be asked.

**Where everything landed.** Build that list from the ledger, not from memory: the Step 4 `landed.py scan --days 1` already refreshed it (it reads git in every DEV repo and file times on Drive and the vault, so files written by scripts and shell copies are included); run `landed.py show --days 1`. Put its project-grouped output in the report under **Landed:** (trim to the projects this session touched if it is long). The ledger lives in `~/.claude/global-memory/landed/` and is pushed with global-memory, so `/landed` on the other machine shows it too.

## Rules

- Push every touched DEV repo. Do not leave the laptop with unpushed work; the other machine pulls from GitHub, not from this disk.
- Never skip Step 3 — memory capture failing silently is the user's top recurring worry.
- If a check fails and the fix is quick and safe (restage a file, clear a stale lock), fix it and note it. If the fix is risky, list it under "Still open" instead.
- Total output should fit on one screen. The user is leaving; brevity is the deliverable.

"""Tests of the draft loop against the formulas in the recovery document.

These check that the code matches the recovered algebra and basic invariants.
They do NOT show the draft matches FAST; no FAST output was available.
Run: PYTHONPATH=research/fast_recon python -m pytest research/fast_recon
"""

import math

import pytest

from recovered_loop import DRAFT_LABEL, Params, circadian, simulate

P = Params()


def day(sleep_from=23.0, sleep_to=7.0, start_hour=0.0, days=1):
    flags = []
    for m in range(days * 1440):
        h = (start_hour + m / 60) % 24
        if sleep_from > sleep_to:  # window wraps midnight
            flags.append(h >= sleep_from or h < sleep_to)
        else:
            flags.append(sleep_from <= h < sleep_to)
    return flags


def test_label_is_visible():
    assert "unvalidated" in DRAFT_LABEL


def test_circadian_matches_formula_at_acrophase():
    # at T = CP the first cosine is 1; second is beta*cos(4*pi*(-p')/24)
    expected = 1 + P.beta * math.cos(4 * math.pi * (-P.phase_offset) / 24)
    assert circadian(P.acrophase) == pytest.approx(expected)


def test_circadian_repeats_every_24_hours():
    assert circadian(5.3) == pytest.approx(circadian(29.3))


def test_starts_at_capacity_minus_350():
    steps = simulate([False], start_hour=12)
    # one awake minute: RT0 - use rate
    assert steps[0].reservoir == pytest.approx(P.reservoir_capacity - 350 - P.use_rate)


def test_awake_depletes_at_use_rate():
    steps = simulate([False] * 600, start_hour=8)
    assert steps[-1].reservoir == pytest.approx(P.reservoir_capacity - 350 - 600 * P.use_rate)


def test_reservoir_stays_in_bounds():
    steps = simulate(day(days=6) + [False] * 8000)
    assert all(0.0 <= s.reservoir <= P.reservoir_capacity for s in steps)


def test_effectiveness_zero_when_reservoir_empty():
    steps = simulate([False] * 20000, start_hour=8)
    assert steps[-1].reservoir == 0.0
    assert steps[-1].effectiveness == 0.0


def test_first_sleep_minutes_do_not_change_reservoir():
    flags = [False] * 60 + [True] * 10
    steps = simulate(flags, start_hour=22)
    before = steps[59].reservoir
    for i in range(60, 60 + P.sleep_freeze):
        assert steps[i].reservoir == pytest.approx(before)
    assert steps[60 + P.sleep_freeze].reservoir > before


def test_sleep_gain_is_capped_at_sleep_max_per_minute():
    flags = [True] * 600
    steps = simulate(flags, start_hour=22)
    gains = [b.reservoir - a.reservoir for a, b in zip(steps, steps[1:])]
    assert max(gains) <= P.sleep_max + 1e-9


def test_inertia_zero_after_window_and_negative_before():
    flags = [True] * 480 + [False] * 400
    steps = simulate(flags, start_hour=23)
    assert steps[480].inertia < 0
    # minute 480 is awake minute ta=1, so ta == window falls on minute 480 + window - 1
    assert steps[480 + P.inertia_window - 1].inertia < 0
    assert steps[480 + P.inertia_window].inertia == 0.0


def test_divisor_applied_to_effectiveness():
    steps = simulate([False], start_hour=12)
    s = steps[0]
    rc = P.reservoir_capacity
    perf = (P.perf_amp_variable * (rc - s.reservoir) / rc + P.perf_amp_fixed) * s.circadian
    expected = (100 * s.reservoir / rc + perf + s.inertia) / P.divisor
    assert s.effectiveness == pytest.approx(expected)


def test_effectiveness_is_clamped():
    steps = simulate(day(days=8))
    assert all(0.0 <= s.effectiveness <= P.effectiveness_cap for s in steps)


def test_more_sleep_beats_less_sleep_next_afternoon():
    long_night = simulate(day(23, 7, days=4) + [False] * 600, start_hour=0)
    short_night = simulate(day(2, 7, days=4) + [False] * 600, start_hour=0)
    assert long_night[-1].reservoir > short_night[-1].reservoir


def test_slow_recovery_off_matches_default():
    flags = day(days=3)
    a = simulate(flags)
    b = simulate(flags, p=Params(slow_recovery=False))
    assert [x.effectiveness for x in a] == [x.effectiveness for x in b]


def test_slow_recovery_lowers_arc_under_heavy_debt():
    # chronic 4-hour nights build debt above K2, so ARc falls and the debt term shrinks
    flags = day(3, 7, days=10)
    on = simulate(flags, p=Params(slow_recovery=True))
    off = simulate(flags)
    assert on[-1].reservoir != off[-1].reservoir

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`; (5) `claude plugin eval` (writing and running plugin eval suites, its JSON/report, sandbox, CI) and the `/skill-doctor` report. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- codex:codex-rescue: Proactively use when Claude Code is stuck, wants a second implementation or diagnosis pass, needs a deeper root-cause investigation, or should hand a substantial coding task to Codex through the shared runtime (Tools: Bash)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ArtifactComments, ArtifactData, ArtifactCheck, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)
- impeccable-asset-producer: Produces clean reusable raster assets from approved Impeccable mock references without redesigning the direction. (Tools: Read, Write, Edit, Bash, Glob, Grep)

- impeccable-documenter: Records DESIGN.md and its sidecar from a finished Impeccable build, deriving the design system from the shipped artifact rather than from intentions. (Tools: Read, Write, Bash, Glob, Grep)

- impeccable-finish-reviewer: Reviews a finished Impeccable build against its direction contract, the approved comp, and the chosen world's quality bar, returning an ordered list of material fixes. (Tools: Read, Bash, Glob, Grep)
- impeccable-manual-edit-applier: Applies leased Impeccable live manual copy-edit batches to source and returns canonical Apply results. (Tools: Read, Write, Edit, Bash, Glob, Grep)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ArtifactComments, ArtifactData, ArtifactCheck, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)
